FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the 
Packaging Codes Sectional Committee had been approved by the Light Mechanical Engineering Division 
Council. 

This standard is useful for the packaging of TV picture tubes/computer monitor tubes for their safe 
handling and transportation by rail, road and sea. 



IS 14312 : 1996 



Indian Standard 

PACKAGING — PACKAGING OF TV 

PICTURE TUBES/COMPUTER MONITOR 

TUBES — CODE OF PRACTICE 



1 SCOPE 

Tins standard lays down the code of practice for the 
packaging of TV picture tubes/computer monitor 
tubes for their sale handling and transportation by 
rail, road and sea. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following standards contain provisions which 
through reference in this text, constitute provision 
of this standard. At the time of publication, the 
editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision, and parties to agreements based 
on this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of 
the standards indicated below:

4 WEIGHT, SIZE AND SHAPE 

4.1 The weight and size of every package shall be 
the minimum practieable to meet the requirements 
having due regard to economy. 



4.2 The shape of the whole package shall be rec- 
tangular. 



4.3 Manufacturers may adopt unit load sizes for 
packaging. IS 14208 : 1995 can be referred for 
dimensions of unit load sizes. 

5 HANDLING FACILITY 

Unless otherwise desired by the purchaser no han- 
dling aid shall be provided on fibreboard con- 
tainers. For plywood and timber containers aid 
shall be as follows:

6 PRE-PACKING TREATMENT 

All picture tubes shall be clean and free from dust, 
dirt, corrosion. 

7 PACKAGING SEQUENCE 

7.1 Frontside (screen) of the picture tube shall be 
wrapped by placing a ring made of cushioning 
material at the centre with polyethylene film and 
t he seams sealed with the adhesive tapes which shall 
not leave any mark on the surface of the picture 
tube/computer monitor tube. Ring is provided to 
protect the picture tubes from scratching. 

7.2 Each TV picture tube/computer monitor tube 
after primary packing shall be further packed in a 
transport package made of fibreboard (corrugated 
and solid) or wood. While selecting the package 
design it shall be ensured that no load is transmitted 
directly on to the primary packs while stacking 
those package during storage. The package design 
shall also ensure that it can withstand all transit 
hazards. 

7.3 Packing in Corrugated Board-Boxes 

7.3.1 Single Unit Packaging 

The cushioning on the bottom of the box shall act 
as base fitting. The picture tube shall be placed on 
the cushion keeping screen side down. The gun end 
shall not in any case protrude outside the box. 
There shall be a minimum gap of 2 cm from the 
top of the box. The space on the top side of the 
box shall be filled by fabricated corrugated 
fibreboard fitment to prevent reorientation of the 
item. IS 10106 (Part 3/Sec 1) : 1984 can be referred. 



7.3,2 Bulk Packaging 

7.3.2.1 In a corrugated fibreboard container, the 
picture tubes shall be located in the fitments of 
cushioning material given in Table 1. There shall 
be no appreciable movement of the supply within 
the fitments when they are abutting or when the 
supply is placed in the container. Suitable arrange- 
ments shall be made to fill the fitments to prevent 
any kind of damage. Top portion of the tubes shall 
be covered with the similar fitments. The 
fibreboard box shall be closed and suitably secured. 

7.3.2.2 On a wooden pallet 

The picture tubes shall be located in the fitments of 
cushioning material and stacked as per the design 
limit.Care shall be taken to adopt suitable arrange- 
ments to prevent misalignment. 

8 MARKING 

8.1 The outer container shall be marked with the 
following information: 

a) Name and address of the manufacturer, 

b) Itcm.no., 

c) Quantity in package, 

d) Information on stacking limit to avoid crus- 
ing, and 

e) Warning and other related informatory 
markings. 

8.2 Standard symbol for indicating fragile con- 
tents with the legend 'HANDLE WITH 
CARE' and the symbol for THIS WAY UP' 
as per IS 1260 (Part 2) : 1979 shall be marked. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality cei ification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also 
reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that 
no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users 
of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by 
referring to the latest issue of 'BIS Handbook' and Standards Monthly Additions*.
